stem: A ticketing company is building an order system for customers in North America, Europe and Asia. It needs a relational schema with SQL, transactions that are strongly consistent everywhere, and write capacity that grows by adding resources rather than by moving to a bigger single primary server. Which database should the team choose?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with cross-region read replicas, which serve reads close to users while one primary takes all writes
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with read pool instances, which add read nodes on demand while the cluster stays in a single region
Spanner with a multi-region instance configuration, which shards data automatically and keeps transactions strongly consistent
Bigtable with clusters in three regions and replication, which spreads reads and writes across clusters in every continent

stem: An energy company collects a reading every few seconds from two million smart meters. The application writes very high volumes of small records and reads them back by meter ID and time range with single-digit millisecond latency. The developers already use the Apache HBase API. Which service fits best?

choices.text: Firestore, with one document per reading stored in a collection per meter and a composite index on the timestamp field
Bigtable, with a row key that starts with the meter ID followed by a timestamp so each meter's readings sit together
BigQuery, with a table partitioned by day and clustered by meter ID so that range scans on recent readings stay quick
Cloud SQL for MySQL, with a table indexed on meter ID and timestamp and several read replicas for the dashboard queries

stem: A firm is moving an internal finance application from its data center to Google Cloud. The application uses Microsoft SQL Server, and the team wants Google to handle backups, patching and high availability failover without changing the database engine. Which service should they use?

choices.text: Cloud SQL for SQL Server, a managed instance that keeps the same engine and adds automated backups and a standby for failover
BigQuery with a dataset per database, a managed warehouse that runs the application's T-SQL transactions without changes
Spanner with the GoogleSQL dialect, a managed database whose schema accepts SQL Server tables after a direct backup restore
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, a managed cluster whose engine takes SQL Server queries after the schema is imported unchanged

stem: A retailer's order application runs on PostgreSQL. Managers want reports that run heavy analytical queries directly on the live order data, without a nightly export, and without slowing down the order transactions. The team wants to keep using standard PostgreSQL clients. Which service should the team choose?

choices.text: Bigtable, with the order data copied into it so that reports can scan wide rows by order date with low latency
Memorystore for Redis, with report results cached in memory so that repeated analytical queries return quickly
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with a scheduled export to Cloud Storage and a BigQuery load job that runs every night
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, using its columnar engine and read pool instances to run the analytical queries on live data

stem: A start-up is building a mobile and web app that stores user profiles and posts as JSON-like documents. The team wants a serverless database that scales automatically without capacity planning, charges for actual use, and works with the Firebase SDKs. Which database should they pick?

choices.text: Bigtable, a wide-column database whose cluster nodes are sized up front and adjusted when traffic changes
Memorystore for Redis, an in-memory store whose hashes hold each profile and post as a set of key fields
Firestore, a serverless document database that scales automatically and integrates with the Firebase platform
Cloud SQL for MySQL, a relational instance with a JSON column type and storage that grows automatically

stem: Analysts at a media company need to run ad hoc SQL queries over several hundred terabytes of clickstream data and connect a BI tool to the results. The team does not want to provision, patch or scale any database servers. Which service should hold the data?

choices.text: Spanner, with a regional instance configuration whose compute capacity is raised before the reporting runs
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, with the largest machine type and read replicas added for each group of analysts
Bigtable, with an instance cluster sized for the full data set and its nodes scaled out during peak query hours
BigQuery, a serverless data warehouse that separates storage from compute and runs SQL queries without servers

stem: A web application on Compute Engine stores user sessions in a Cloud SQL database, and page loads slow down under heavy traffic. The developers already use an open source Redis client library and want a managed in-memory store that answers in under a millisecond, reached over a private IP in their VPC. What should they use?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, a managed Redis-protocol store that the existing client can use with no code changes
Firestore in Native mode, a managed document store that the existing client reaches through its MongoDB API
A Cloud SQL read replica, a managed copy of the database that the existing client reaches over the same private IP
Bigtable with an SSD cluster, a managed wide-column store that the existing client reaches through its HBase API

stem: A logistics company runs dozens of services that produce and consume events with Apache Kafka client libraries and Kafka Connect, on a self-managed cluster. They want Google Cloud to run the cluster for them without rewriting producers or consumers. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, whose streams store the events and accept the existing Kafka producer calls with no code changes
Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka, which runs Kafka clusters that the existing Kafka clients connect to
Pub/Sub, whose topics and subscriptions receive the existing Kafka producer and consumer calls with no code changes
Dataflow, whose streaming jobs act as Kafka brokers that the existing Kafka clients connect to as their bootstrap servers

stem: A game studio wants to collect gameplay events from thousands of game servers, enrich and aggregate them in near real time, and write the results into BigQuery. The team wants fully managed services with no clusters to run. Which TWO services should they combine? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Memorystore for Redis, to hold the raw events in memory and run the enrichment and aggregation step in the cache
Filestore, to collect the events as files on a shared NFS share that BigQuery reads directly as the source table
Dataflow, to run a streaming Apache Beam pipeline that reads the events, transforms them and writes to BigQuery
Cloud SQL for MySQL, to stage every raw event in a table and run scheduled stored procedures that load BigQuery
Pub/Sub, to receive the events asynchronously from the game servers and buffer them for downstream processing

stem: A media team runs a rendering application on a managed instance group of Linux VMs and on a GKE cluster. All VMs and Pods must read and write the same POSIX file tree at the same time over NFS, with file locking. Which storage should the team provision?

choices.text: A Cloud Storage bucket mounted with Cloud Storage FUSE, which provides file locking and full POSIX semantics
A Filestore instance, whose NFS file share every VM and Pod can mount read-write at the same time
A Memorystore for Redis instance, whose keys each hold one file so that every VM and Pod reads the same data
A zonal Persistent Disk attached to every VM, which mounts it read-write as a shared POSIX file system

stem: An engineering firm is moving Windows file servers to Google Cloud. Users on Windows desktops map the shares as network drives over SMB, and Linux build servers mount other volumes over NFS. The firm wants one fully managed service that provides both protocols. Which service should they choose?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, mounting its parallel file system on both the Windows desktops and the build servers
Cloud Storage with Cloud Storage FUSE, mounting each bucket as a network drive on the Windows desktops over SMB
Filestore, using the regional tier for continuous availability and mounting the shares from Windows over SMB
Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, which provides managed volumes over SMB and NFS protocols with snapshots and backups

stem: A research lab trains large machine learning models on hundreds of GPU VMs and GKE nodes. Training needs a shared POSIX file system that delivers very high aggregate throughput and IOPS to all nodes at once, and data sets are staged from Cloud Storage. Which storage service is designed for this?

choices.text: Google Cloud Managed Lustre, a fully managed parallel file system for AI and HPC with transfers to and from Cloud Storage
Cloud Storage with the Nearline storage class, a bucket that every GPU node reads through the JSON API during training
Filestore with the basic tier, a legacy managed NFS share for basic file sharing that every GPU node mounts at once
Memorystore for Redis with five replicas, an in-memory store whose keys hold the training files for every GPU node

stem: A finance team continuously uploads transaction exports to a bucket and runs an analysis job on them about once a month. The files must stay online with fast access, and the team wants to lower at-rest storage cost without paying for retrievals more often than needed. Which storage class should the bucket use by default?

choices.text: Standard storage, which is meant for data read less than once a year and has a 365-day minimum storage duration
Nearline storage, which is meant for data read or modified about once a month and has a 30-day minimum storage duration
Archive storage, which is meant for data read about once a month and has offline retrieval that takes several hours
Coldline storage, which is meant for data read or modified several times every week and has no minimum storage duration

stem: A hospital must keep scanned records for ten years for regulatory reasons. The records are almost never read, but during an audit some files must be readable at once. The team is evaluating Archive storage. Which TWO statements about Archive storage are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An object deleted or replaced before it has been stored for 365 days is charged as if it was stored for 365 days
Objects in Archive storage must first be restored to Standard storage, which can take several hours per object
Archive storage can be used only in single-region buckets, so it cannot be combined with dual-region redundancy
Archive storage cannot be set as a bucket's default class, so each object must get the class when it is uploaded
Objects in Archive storage are readable within milliseconds, with no restore step before the data can be accessed

stem: A bucket holds 2 TB of log files in Standard storage. An engineer changes the bucket's default storage class to Coldline to save money, but a week later every existing object still shows the Standard class. What explains this, and how can the engineer change the existing objects?

choices.text: The default class is ignored while uniform bucket-level access is on; disable it so the existing objects can take the new default class
The change takes up to 30 days to reach existing objects; wait for the background conversion to finish before checking the class again
The bucket is in a multi-region, where Coldline is not supported; recreate the bucket in a single region and then copy the objects there
The default class applies only to objects added later; rewrite the existing objects with gcloud storage objects update and --storage-class

stem: An engineer must upload a local directory of about 200 GB with many subdirectories from a workstation into gs://proj-media-raw, keeping the folder structure, and the objects should be stored as Nearline. The network link is good. Which command is the simplest correct choice?

choices.text: bq load --source_format=CSV proj_media.raw ./media/* --storage_class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp ./media gs://proj-media-raw --no-clobber --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage cp --recursive ./media gs://proj-media-raw --storage-class=NEARLINE
gcloud storage buckets create gs://proj-media-raw --placement=./media --default-storage-class=NEARLINE

stem: A company keeps 400 TB of product images in Amazon S3 and wants to move them to Cloud Storage, then copy new and changed files every night until the cut-over. The team wants a managed service that retries failures and checks integrity, without writing scripts or running copy servers. What should they use?

choices.text: A BigQuery load job from the S3 bucket each night, followed by an export of the loaded data to Cloud Storage
A Compute Engine VM that runs gcloud storage rsync from the S3 bucket every night through a cron job on the VM
Storage Transfer Service, with an S3 source, a Cloud Storage destination and a daily schedule for the transfer job
Transfer Appliance, shipped to the S3 region so that the images are copied onto it and loaded into Cloud Storage

stem: An analyst runs bq load to load CSV files from gs://acme-sales-us/2026/*.csv into the table sales.daily. The bucket is in the US multi-region, and the sales dataset was created in the europe-west1 region. The load job fails before reading any rows. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The bucket and dataset are in different locations; copy the files to a bucket colocated with the dataset, or load into a dataset in the bucket's location
The table needs an explicit schema file for CSV loads; pass a local JSON schema file because schema auto-detection cannot read CSV
The analyst needs Storage Transfer Service between Cloud Storage and BigQuery; create a transfer job, because bq load cannot read buckets
Wildcards are not supported in Cloud Storage URIs for bq load; list every CSV file by name in a comma-separated list of URIs instead

stem: Each night a job drops a CSV file with one header row into gs://acme-orders/daily/. An engineer writes a bq load command that adds the file's rows to the existing table orders.history, which has a schema and holds years of data that must not be lost. Which TWO choices must the command make? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Pass --time_partitioning_type=DAY on each run so that the existing table is converted to daily partitions
Pass --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON so that the header line is read as the names of the columns
Pass --replace so that the existing schema is kept and new rows are written alongside the old data
Use --skip_leading_rows=1 so that the header row is not loaded as a data row into the table
Append the rows, by passing --noreplace or by leaving out --replace, so that existing rows stay

stem: A payments company stores transaction receipts in Cloud Storage. The bucket must keep serving reads and writes with the same bucket name if one region goes down, the data must stay in two regions the company chooses, and newly written objects must be copied to the second region within 15 minutes. Which TWO settings meet these needs when the bucket is created? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A single-region location, with Autoclass enabled so that objects move to colder classes in a second region over time
The recovery point objective set to ASYNC_TURBO, which turns on turbo replication for the dual-region bucket
A multi-region location such as EU, with turbo replication enabled so that copies reach a second region in minutes
A single-region location, with Object Versioning enabled so that earlier versions of objects can be restored later
A dual-region location, either a predefined pair or a configurable dual-region whose two regions are set with --placement

stem: A logistics company is moving a legacy inventory application to Google Cloud. The application runs on a commercial Linux distribution, loads a vendor-supplied kernel driver at boot, and the vendor supports it only when it runs unmodified on a full operating system. The team wants to change as little as possible. Where should the team run the application?

choices.text: On a GKE Autopilot cluster, running the application as a Deployment with the vendor driver installed through an init container in each Pod
On Cloud Run, after packaging the application and its kernel driver into a container image that loads the driver when each instance starts
On Cloud Run functions, splitting the application into event-driven functions that call the vendor driver through a shared library at runtime
On Compute Engine VMs built from an image of that distribution, so the team controls the operating system, kernel modules and installed packages

stem: A small team has a stateless REST API packaged as a container image. It receives traffic only during office hours and none at night or on weekends. The team does not want to manage VMs or clusters and does not want to pay for compute while the API is idle. Which compute option should the team choose?

choices.text: A Cloud Run service deployed from the image, letting it scale to zero instances when no requests arrive
A regional managed instance group of small VMs running the container, autoscaled on average CPU utilization with a minimum of zero
A GKE Standard cluster with the cluster autoscaler enabled on its node pool, running the image as a Deployment behind a Service
An Agent Runtime deployment on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which runs the image in a fully managed environment

stem: A developer has built a customer-support AI agent and now needs to run it in production. The team wants a fully managed environment that deploys and scales the agent, keeps conversation state across turns, can store long-term memories about users, and provides tracing and logging, without the team operating servers. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Split each agent tool into a separate Cloud Run function and keep the conversation history in the instance memory of each function
Deploy the agent to Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and use Agent Platform Sessions and Memory Bank for state
Package the agent as a container and run it on a Compute Engine managed instance group, storing session state in a Cloud SQL database the team manages
Run the agent on a GKE Standard cluster with a StatefulSet that stores each conversation on the Persistent Disk of its Pod

stem: An engineer created a reporting VM with a script copied from an old wiki that included --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE and --no-restart-on-failure. Last night Google performed host maintenance, and this morning the VM is in the TERMINATED state and nobody restarted it. The VM uses a general-purpose machine type with no GPUs. How should the engineer change the VM's host maintenance policy?

choices.text: Enable deletion protection on the VM so that Compute Engine can no longer stop or terminate it during host maintenance events
Recreate the VM as a Spot VM so that Compute Engine moves it to another host automatically whenever maintenance is scheduled
Set the maintenance behavior to migrate (live migration) and turn automatic restart back on so host errors also restart the VM
Add a snapshot schedule to the boot disk so that the VM is recreated from the latest snapshot after each maintenance event

stem: A data team plans to use Spot VMs to cut the cost of a nightly transcoding fleet. Which statements about Spot VMs are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Spot VMs are covered by the Compute Engine SLA at a reduced uptime percentage, so short outages caused by preemption earn service credits
Spot VMs are priced by bidding: you set a maximum hourly bid, and the VM is preempted whenever the market price rises above your bid
Spot VMs cannot live migrate during host maintenance and cannot be configured to restart automatically when a host event occurs
Spot VMs keep running for at most 24 hours, after which Compute Engine always stops them, even when spare capacity is still available
Compute Engine can preempt a Spot VM at any time to reclaim capacity, and its termination action decides whether the VM is stopped or deleted

stem: A media startup renders video frames pulled from a work queue. Each frame is independent and can simply be retried, and the goal is the lowest compute cost. When Compute Engine reclaims a worker VM, the team wants a replacement worker created automatically from the same configuration without anyone stepping in. What should the team set up?

choices.text: Standard VMs on a sole-tenant node group, with the automatic restart policy enabled so that crashed workers come back
An unmanaged instance group of Spot VMs, each created by hand, with a load balancer health check pointed at the group
One large Spot VM with automatic restart turned on, so that Compute Engine restarts it on another host after preemption
A managed instance group whose instance template uses the Spot provisioning model, so the group recreates preempted VMs

stem: A team creates Spot VMs each night with gcloud compute instances create ... --provisioning-model=SPOT. After preemptions, dozens of VMs remain in the TERMINATED state, and their boot disks keep adding to the bill. The team wants preempted VMs to disappear on their own. Which change should they make to the create command?

choices.text: Add --no-restart-on-failure so that Compute Engine does not try to bring the Spot VM back after it is preempted
Add --instance-termination-action=DELETE so that Compute Engine deletes each Spot VM when it preempts it
Replace --provisioning-model=SPOT with --preemptible so that preempted VMs are removed after 24 hours of running
Add --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE so that preempted VMs are terminated permanently instead of only stopped

stem: A finance team runs a third-party risk engine licensed per vCPU; they own licenses for exactly 6 vCPUs. Load tests show the engine needs 6 vCPUs and about 30 GB of memory. The closest predefined type, n2-standard-8, would need 8 licenses. What should the cloud engineer create?

choices.text: A VM with an N2 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM with the predefined n2-highmem-4 machine type and 32 GB of memory
A VM with a C3 custom machine type of 6 vCPUs and 30 GB of memory
A VM on a sole-tenant node with 8 vCPUs, reserving 2 vCPUs for later

stem: An in-memory analytics product is licensed per vCPU, and the team has budgeted for 4 vCPUs. The data set needs 64 GB of RAM on a single VM, and CPU usage is low. The team plans to use the N2 machine series. Which configuration meets both constraints?

choices.text: The predefined n2-highmem-8 type with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB, then license only 4 of the vCPUs in the product
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, created with the extended memory feature
An E2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, since E2 has no memory-per-vCPU limit
An N2 custom machine type with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of memory, the most memory a 4-vCPU custom type allows

stem: A team runs a self-managed PostgreSQL server on one Compute Engine VM in us-central1-a. Management now requires that the database survive the loss of that zone with no loss of committed data, and a standby VM can be kept stopped in us-central1-b. Which storage design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with a snapshot schedule every hour, and create a new disk in us-central1-b from the latest snapshot
Keep the data on a zonal Hyperdisk Balanced volume with Asynchronous Replication to europe-west1, and fail over to a VM created in that region
Keep the data on Local SSD disks in RAID 0 for speed, and copy the database files to a Cloud Storage bucket in the same region every fifteen minutes
Keep the data on a Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability or regional Persistent Disk volume replicated to both zones, and attach it to the standby VM on failover

stem: A MySQL VM keeps 400 GB of data on a balanced Persistent Disk and is limited by disk IOPS. To get the IOPS it needs, the team would have to grow the disk to several terabytes it will never fill. The VM's machine series supports Hyperdisk. Which option raises IOPS without paying for unused capacity?

choices.text: Move the data to a Hyperdisk Throughput volume and raise its IOPS level separately from its size
Resize the balanced Persistent Disk to several terabytes, since disk IOPS scale with its capacity
Move the data to a Hyperdisk Balanced volume and set the provisioned IOPS independently of its size
Move the data to Local SSD disks, which deliver higher IOPS than any network-attached disk type

stem: An inference fleet of 400 Compute Engine VMs must load the same 150 GB of model weights at startup. The weights never change between releases, and startup time matters. The team wants one copy of the data that every VM reads directly as a disk. Which disk type should they use?

choices.text: A Hyperdisk ML volume, loaded once and then attached in read-only mode to every VM in the fleet
A Hyperdisk Balanced volume in multi-writer mode, attached to every VM in the fleet at the same time
A Hyperdisk Throughput volume, attached to one VM that copies the weights to the others over the network
A Hyperdisk Extreme volume, attached in read-write mode to every VM in the fleet for the highest IOPS

stem: A team plans to add Local SSD to a Microsoft SQL Server VM. Which statements about Local SSD are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Local SSD cannot be used as a boot volume, so the VM still needs a durable boot disk such as Hyperdisk or Persistent Disk
Local SSD is synchronously replicated to a second zone, so its data survives the failure of the zone that hosts the VM
Local SSD data is kept when a Spot VM is preempted, because the disks stay attached to the stopped VM on the same host
Local SSD disks can be detached from a running VM and attached to another VM in the same zone, like a Hyperdisk volume
Local SSD gives the fastest block storage but is temporary, so it suits scratch data and caches such as SQL Server tempdb

stem: A web tier runs in a managed instance group created from the instance template web-tmpl-v1, which uses e2-medium. The team wants new and existing VMs to use n2-standard-2, but finds no way to edit the machine type of web-tmpl-v1. What is the correct approach?

choices.text: Delete web-tmpl-v1 while the group is still using it, then recreate a template with the same name and the new machine type
Run gcloud compute instance-templates update web-tmpl-v1 with the new machine type, then restart the VMs in the group one by one
Stop each VM in the group, change its machine type to n2-standard-2 directly, and start it again so the template no longer matters
Create a new template, such as web-tmpl-v2 based on the old one with n2-standard-2, and roll it out to the group with an update

stem: A managed instance group autoscales on average CPU utilization with a 60% target. Each new VM spends about 4 minutes installing packages at boot, with high CPU, before the app serves traffic. During every spike the group overshoots and adds far more VMs than needed. Which autoscaler setting should be adjusted?

choices.text: Configure scale-in controls with a small maximum allowed reduction, so that the group adds fewer VMs during each spike
Set the initialization period to about 240 seconds, so that scale-out ignores data from VMs that are still starting up
Raise the target CPU utilization to 95%, so that the high CPU of booting VMs no longer triggers additional scale-out
Set the stabilization period to 4 minutes, so that the autoscaler waits that long before it adds any new VMs to the group

stem: Workers in a managed instance group process messages from a Pub/Sub subscription. The group autoscales on average CPU utilization, and the team set the minimum number of instances to 0 so it would be empty overnight when the queue is empty, yet at least one VM always keeps running. How should the team reach zero instances when there is no work?

choices.text: Switch the signal to HTTP load balancing serving capacity, which reports zero usage once all requests have stopped
Add a scaling schedule with a capacity of 0 instances every night, which forces the group to delete all of its VMs
Scale on a Cloud Monitoring metric for the subscription's backlog of undelivered messages instead of CPU, keeping minimum at 0
Lower the CPU utilization target to 1%, so that the autoscaler sees even one idle VM as over target and removes it

stem: A retailer's web tier runs on Compute Engine. It must keep serving if an entire zone in us-east1 goes down, and VMs on which the web application has hung (while the VM itself still runs) must be replaced automatically. Which configuration meets these goals? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure application-based autohealing with a health check on the app's endpoint, so the group recreates unhealthy VMs
Rely on the load balancer's health check alone, since a failing backend health check makes the group recreate the VM
Keep automatic restart enabled in the VMs' host maintenance policy, so that Compute Engine restarts VMs whose app hangs
Put the VMs in an unmanaged instance group that contains VMs from all three zones of us-east1 behind the load balancer
Create a regional managed instance group so that the group's VMs are spread across several zones of us-east1

stem: A project's Linux VMs use SSH keys stored in project metadata. The security team wants contractors to get SSH access through IAM, without sudo, and to lose access automatically as soon as their IAM role is removed. Which actions should the cloud engineer take? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Add each contractor's public SSH key to the project metadata and set an expiry time on every key that is added
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to TRUE in the project metadata so that the project's VMs use OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osAdminLogin role so that they can log in to the VMs through OS Login
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 role so that they can manage SSH keys on the instances
Grant the contractors the roles/compute.osLogin role on the project or on the specific VMs they need to reach

stem: A project still uses metadata-based SSH keys, and a dozen administrators have their keys in project metadata. One new VM processes payroll data and must accept only the two keys that the payroll team adds to that VM's own metadata. OS Login cannot be used yet. What should the engineer configure on the VM?

choices.text: Remove the dozen administrator keys from the project metadata, and add the two payroll keys to the project metadata instead
Create the payroll VM without a service account, so that the keys stored in project metadata are not copied onto the VM
Set the metadata key block-project-ssh-keys to TRUE on the payroll VM, and add the two payroll keys to its instance metadata
Set the metadata key enable-oslogin to FALSE on the payroll VM, so that it reads only the keys stored in its own metadata

stem: An operations team set up VM Manager and a weekly patch deployment for 200 Ubuntu VMs. Patch compliance reports show up for every VM, but patch jobs fail on the VMs that have no external IP address; their subnet has no Cloud NAT and no proxy. What should the team do?

choices.text: Grant the OS Config agent's service account the Compute Admin role on the project, so it can download patches for the VMs
Recreate the failing VMs with external IP addresses, since VM Manager requires every managed VM to have a public address
Switch the patch deployment to OS inventory management, which installs updates without contacting package repositories
Give the VMs a path to package updates, such as Cloud NAT for the subnet or a local repository the VMs can reach

stem: A security team requires that a specific monitoring package be installed on every Linux VM labeled env=prod, and that it be reinstalled automatically if someone removes it. The team wants to use a VM Manager feature rather than writing its own tooling. Which feature should it use?

choices.text: OS policies, which describe the desired package state for the selected VMs and keep that state in place
A startup script in the instance metadata of each production VM that installs the package at every boot
OS inventory management, which collects and reports which packages are present on each selected VM
Patch deployments, which apply operating system updates to the selected VMs on a recurring schedule

stem: A research group will train a large recommendation model. The model is dominated by matrix multiplications, uses ultra-large embeddings, has no custom operations in its training loop, and is expected to train for weeks with large batch sizes. Which hardware should the cloud engineer plan for?

choices.text: GPUs attached to Compute Engine VMs, because GPUs are the only accelerator that Google Cloud offers for model training
High-CPU Compute Engine VMs, because large embeddings run best on general-purpose CPUs with plenty of cores
Cloud TPUs, because they suit models whose training loop relies on many custom PyTorch operations run on CPUs
Cloud TPUs, because they are ASICs built for large matrix operations and suit large models that train for weeks

stem: A platform team lets developers create their own projects. Each new project must be paid for by the company's central Cloud Billing account, but developers must not see invoices, change payment methods or manage who has access to that billing account. Which role should the developers get on the billing account, in addition to Project Creator on their folder?

choices.text: Billing Account Creator (`roles/billing.creator`), which allows creating new self-serve billing accounts at the organization level
Billing Account Administrator (`roles/billing.admin`), which allows linking projects and also manages the account's settings
Billing Account User (`roles/billing.user`), which allows linking projects to the account and has very restricted permissions
Billing Account Viewer (`roles/billing.viewer`), which allows reading cost data and transactions recorded on the billing account

stem: The finance department wants two analysts to see the costs, transactions and payment documents of the company's Cloud Billing account. They must not be able to link or unlink projects, create budgets or change any account settings. Which predefined role on the billing account fits this best?

choices.text: Project Billing Manager, which is granted on each project and lets the analysts view that project's invoices directly
Billing Account Viewer, which gives read access to cost and payment information without managing the billing account
Billing Account Costs Manager, which shows cost information and also lets the analysts create, edit and delete budgets
Billing Account User, which lets the analysts attach projects to the account while hiding its payment information

stem: A FinOps engineer must create and edit budgets for every project on the billing account and set up the usage cost export to BigQuery. Security policy says the engineer must not link or unlink projects or manage who has access to the billing account. Which role should be granted on the billing account?

choices.text: Billing Account Costs Manager, which manages budgets and the export of cost data but cannot link projects or manage account properties
Billing Account Viewer, which reads cost data and transactions and can edit budgets that other administrators already created
Project Billing Costs Manager, which manages budgets and the cost export for every project linked to the billing account without project roles
Billing Account Administrator, which manages budgets and the export of cost data and also controls the account's role assignments

stem: A project owner wants a contractor to move the project `web-prod` from an old Cloud Billing account to a new one. The contractor must not get access to any resources in the project. Which roles give the contractor what is needed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Billing Account Viewer (`roles/billing.viewer`) on the new Cloud Billing account only
Project Editor (`roles/editor`) on the `web-prod` project to change its settings

The gcp.resourceLocations constraint with the allowed value eu, so that the eu multi-region and every individual European region below it are permitted
The compute.vmExternalIpAccess constraint with a list of EU instances, so that only virtual machines located in European zones are allowed to start
The gcp.resourceLocations constraint with the allowed value in:eu-locations, so that every location in the Google-curated EU value group is permitted

stem: A Google Cloud organization was created in 2025. A project owner tries to grant the Viewer role on her project to an external consultant who uses a personal gmail.com account, and the grant fails with an error that the member doesn't belong to a permitted customer. No one in the company remembers configuring such a rule. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The Viewer role is a basic role, and basic roles can't be granted to accounts outside the organization unless an IAM Condition is attached to the grant
The consultant must first accept a Cloud Identity invitation, because personal Google accounts are rejected until they join the company's domain
The Domain restricted sharing constraint (iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains) is enforced on the organization as part of the Google Cloud security baseline
The project's IAM policy already contains the maximum number of role bindings, so new members can only be added after unused bindings are removed

stem: The Platform folder has an organization policy for the list constraint compute.trustedImageProjects that denies projects/legacy-images. A project under that folder sets its own policy with inheritFromParent set to true and allows projects/legacy-images. A developer in the project still can't create a VM from an image in legacy-images. Why?

choices.text: A project-level policy can only add values to the deny list, because projects are not allowed to override any constraint set by an ancestor folder
The project's policy takes up to 24 hours to replace the folder's policy, and until then the folder's denial of the image project stays in effect for it
The policies are merged because the project inherits from its parent, and for list rules a denied value always takes precedence over an allowed value
The allowed value must use the under: prefix instead of the plain project path, because list values without a prefix are silently ignored

stem: The Production folder enforces the boolean constraint compute.disableSerialPortAccess. During an audit, the security team finds that one project in the folder has VMs with serial port access enabled, created after the policy was set. Organization policies for that project show a policy for the same constraint. What explains the finding?

choices.text: The project has its own policy that sets enforce to false for the constraint, and for boolean rules the project's own value replaces the inherited one
The VMs were created by a service account, and organization policy constraints apply only to requests that human users make in the console
The folder's policy only applies to projects created after it was set, so projects that already existed in the folder are never covered by it
Boolean constraints are evaluated by merging all ancestors, and a single enforce true anywhere above the project should have blocked these VMs

stem: On Monday, an administrator enforces the gcp.resourceLocations constraint at the organization to allow only in:europe-west1-locations. On Tuesday, the team finds that Cloud Storage buckets created last month in us-central1 still exist and still serve data. What is the reason?

choices.text: The buckets are protected by uniform bucket-level access, which exempts a bucket from any organization policy set at a higher level
The constraint restricts the creation of new resources at runtime and does not remove or block resources that existed before the policy
Organization policies need 72 hours to propagate across all projects, after which the existing buckets in us-central1 will be deleted
The constraint only applies to Compute Engine resources, so Cloud Storage buckets are never evaluated against the allowed locations list

stem: The security team wants to enforce a new organization policy that blocks external IPv4 addresses on VMs across the organization, but first wants to see which current workflows would break, without blocking anyone yet. What should they do?

choices.text: Enforce the policy with inheritFromParent set to false at the organization, which logs the violations for a week before denials actually start
Run gcloud org-policies describe with the --effective flag for each project, which lists every API call that the proposed policy would reject
Grant all developers the Organization Policy Viewer role so that each team receives an email listing its own resources that break the policy
Create the organization policy in dry-run mode, then review the audit logs for violations that would have been denied before switching it to enforced

stem: A company requires that no VM anywhere in its organization receives an external IPv4 address, including VMs created by project Owners. Which control enforces this requirement?

choices.text: Removing the Compute Instance Admin role from all developers in each project, so that only project Owners can still create VMs with any configuration
A VPC firewall rule in each project that denies all egress traffic to 0.0.0.0/0, so that VMs with external addresses can never reach the internet
An organization policy at the organization for compute.vmExternalIpAccess that denies all values, which applies to every VM creation request regardless of role
An IAM Condition on every project's Owner role binding that only allows the role when the requested VM configuration has no external IPv4 address

stem: A team lead must give the data-analysts group read-only access to everything in project sales-prod by using the gcloud CLI, without changing any of the project's existing role grants. Which command should the lead run?

choices.text: gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding sales-prod --member="user:data-analysts@example.com" --role="roles/viewer"
gcloud projects set-iam-policy sales-prod --member="group:data-analysts@example.com" --role="roles/viewer"
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding sales-prod --member="group:data-analysts@example.com" --role="viewer"
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding sales-prod --member="group:data-analysts@example.com" --role="roles/viewer"

stem: A company runs Microsoft Active Directory on premises as the source of truth for employees and groups. It wants the same users and groups to exist in Cloud Identity automatically, kept up to date when HR changes Active Directory, and wants users to sign in with their Active Directory passwords. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Configure Google Cloud Directory Sync to copy password hashes from Cloud Identity back into Active Directory after each run
Configure SAML single sign-on so that Cloud Identity delegates user authentication to Active Directory, for example through AD FS
Create each user manually in the Google Admin console and ask employees to keep their Google password the same as their AD one
Configure Cloud Identity as the authoritative source and let Active Directory pull user changes from Cloud Identity every hour
Run Google Cloud Directory Sync on a server with LDAP access to Active Directory as a scheduled task to provision users and groups

stem: A contractor, lee@example.com, needs to be a member of the Google group gcp-analysts@example.com for the next 30 days only. The group already holds the roles the contractor needs on several projects. Which gcloud command adds the contractor so that the membership ends on its own?

choices.text: gcloud identity groups memberships add --group-email="gcp-analysts@example.com" --member-email="lee@example.com" --expiration="30d"
gcloud identity groups create gcp-analysts@example.com --organization="example.com" --member-email="lee@example.com" --expiration="30d"
gcloud identity groups memberships add --group-email="lee@example.com" --member-email="gcp-analysts@example.com" --roles="EXPIRE_30D"
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding analytics-prod --member="group:gcp-analysts@example.com" --role="roles/viewer" --expiration="30d"

stem: A project Owner who also holds Organization Viewer on the organization opens the Groups page in the Google Cloud console to create a group for her team, but she can't create it. Her IAM roles look correct. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: She also needs the Owner role on the organization resource, because group creation uses the resourcemanager permissions of the organization
Groups can only be created from the gcloud CLI, and the Groups page in the console is read-only for every user regardless of permissions
Permissions to create and manage groups are managed by Google Workspace or Cloud Identity administration, not IAM, and she lacks them
The organization has no Google Cloud billing account linked, and groups can't be created until a billing account is linked to the organization

stem: A developer with the Viewer role on project ml-sandbox runs gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com and gets a permission denied error. The project lead wants to give her the narrowest predefined role that lets her enable and disable APIs in this project. Which role should be granted?

choices.text: Browser (roles/browser) on the organization, which includes the permissions to list and enable services in all of the organization's projects
Service Usage Admin (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin) on the project, which includes the permissions to enable and disable services
Project Creator (roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator) on the project, which includes the permissions to enable services on projects she can see
Service Usage Consumer (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer) on the project, which includes the permissions to enable and use services

stem: To reduce clutter, an administrator plans to disable APIs that look unused in an old project: Cloud Storage, Cloud Run and Kubernetes Engine. Before doing so, she checks what disabling each API does to existing resources. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Disabling the Kubernetes Engine API suspends running clusters, and suspended clusters are deleted after 30 days unless the API is re-enabled
Disabling the Cloud Run API keeps existing Cloud Run services serving traffic and only blocks new deployments and revisions until it is re-enabled
Disabling the Cloud Storage API deletes all buckets in the project after a 7-day grace period, so the data must be exported beforehand
Disabling any API immediately cancels every pending fee and all billable usage of that service, so it is a safe way to stop costs at once
Disabling the Cloud Storage API leaves the stored objects in place, so storage charges continue until the data itself is deleted

stem: A company runs VMs in two projects, shop-staging and shop-prod. The operations team wants one place in Cloud Monitoring to chart and alert on the metrics of both projects, without having to filter out unrelated resources. What should they configure?

choices.text: Create a folder that contains both projects and enable Cloud Monitoring on the folder, which then charts the metrics of all child projects
Create a log sink in each project that routes all metrics to a shared BigQuery dataset, and build charts and alerts on that dataset instead
Add shop-staging to the metrics scope of shop-prod, and build all charts and alerting policies in shop-prod, which already hosts the production VMs
Create a new project with no resources, such as shop-monitoring, and add shop-staging and shop-prod to the metrics scope of that scoping project

stem: An SRE holds Monitoring Admin on the scoping project ops-central. When she tries to add the project billing-api to the metrics scope of ops-central, the operation fails with a permission error. She holds only Monitoring Viewer on billing-api. What should be changed?

choices.text: Grant her Logging Admin on billing-api, because adding a project to a metrics scope first creates a log sink in the project being added
Grant her Monitoring Admin on the organization only, because metrics scope changes are always authorized at the organization resource level
Grant her Monitoring Admin on billing-api as well, because modifying a metrics scope needs that role on the scoping project and on each added project
Grant her the Project IAM Admin role on ops-central, because metrics scope membership is stored as an IAM binding on the scoping project

stem: A team's deployment script fails when it tries to create 20 more VMs in us-central1, with an error that the regional CPUS quota is exceeded. The team needs the capacity in that region next week. What should the team do?

choices.text: Buy a paid Customer Care support package first, because quota increase requests can only be submitted by customers who have paid support
Raise the monthly budget amount on the project's billing account, because Compute Engine sets each regional CPU quota from the current budget amount
Remove the gcp.resourceLocations organization policy from the project, because regional quotas are calculated from the locations that the policy allows
In the console's Quotas & System Limits page, edit the CPUs quota for us-central1 and submit an adjustment request, using an account with the Quota Administrator role

stem: A new cloud engineer is learning how quotas and limits work in Google Cloud. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Zonal resource usage never counts against a regional quota, so creating VMs in one zone can't reduce the quota left in other zones
System limits, such as maximum file sizes or database schema limits, are fixed and can't be increased through a quota adjustment request
Rate quotas are released only when the resources that consumed them are deleted, in the same way that allocation quotas are released
Quota values are identical in every project of an organization, so increasing a quota in one project raises it for all other projects
Most quotas apply per project, so using a resource in one project doesn't reduce the quota that is available in another project

stem: An analytics project has run for over a year, and its usage of several Compute Engine quotas grows steadily. The team keeps hitting quota values and filing increase requests by hand. They want Google Cloud to request modest increases automatically when peak usage approaches the quota. What should they use?

choices.text: Enable the quota adjuster for the project, which monitors supported quotas and requests increases when peak usage approaches the quota value
Move the project into a folder with an organization-level quota override, which raises the project's quotas whenever folder usage grows
Set every quota in the project to the highest value shown in the console, so that the project never reaches a quota value in the future
Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy on quota usage, which automatically files an increase request whenever the alert condition is met

stem: Two founders of a new startup sign up for a Google Cloud Free Trial for the first time with a Google email address. They have no Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account and no DNS domain yet, but they want an organization resource so they can use folders and organization policies from day one. What should they expect?

choices.text: They must open a support case to request an organization, because Google creates organization resources for Free Trial customers only on request
They must buy a domain and sign up for Cloud Identity Free first, because an organization resource can only be created for a verified DNS domain
They can create folders directly under their "No organization" projects, and an organization resource is created later when a domain is verified
A standalone organization is created automatically when the new account signs in and accepts the terms, and the account owner gets the Organization Owner role

stem: The only Organization Owner of a standalone organization wants to avoid a single point of failure if she leaves the company. She plans how to add more owners. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A user in a workforce identity pool can be invited as an Organization Owner by entering the user's workforce pool principal identifier
Any principal with Organization Administrator can add new Organization Owners by granting roles/cloudowner.admin with gcloud add-iam-policy-binding
A service account can be invited as an Organization Owner so that automation keeps the organization manageable if every human owner leaves
Each standalone organization can have only one Organization Owner, so the owner must transfer the role instead of adding a second owner
An invited principal becomes an Organization Owner only after accepting the emailed invitation, which must happen within 30 days

stem: A company is creating projects for production workloads that will connect to its on-premises network, which uses 10.128.0.0/16 among other ranges. The network team wants every new production project to start with no network, so that they can create custom mode VPCs with planned ranges. What should be configured?

choices.text: Delete the default firewall rules after each project is created, because the default network only becomes an auto mode network through those rules
Convert each project's custom mode default network to auto mode after creation, so that the subnet ranges are then chosen by the network team
Enforce the compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation constraint on the Production folder, so that new projects there are created without the default network
Keep the default network in each project, because its auto mode subnets can be peered with on-premises networks that use overlapping ranges

stem: An engineer plans to deploy VMs of machine type c4d-standard-4 and wants to know which regions and zones offer that machine type before choosing a location. Which gcloud command answers this?

choices.text: gcloud compute regions describe c4d-standard-4 --format=json
gcloud compute machine-types list --filter="name=c4d-standard-4"
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name=c4d-standard-4"
gcloud compute zones list --filter="name=c4d-standard-4"

stem: A cost review asks the platform team to list every Compute Engine VM, across all projects in the organization, that has a cost-center label set to any value. They want a quick, interactive search without exporting data anywhere. Which command should they use?

choices.text: gcloud projects list --filter="labels.cost-center:*" --format="value(projectId)" --organization=ORG_ID --sort-by=name
gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels.cost-center:*" --project=ORG_ID --format="table(name,zone,labels)"
gcloud asset export --organization=ORG_ID --asset-types=compute.googleapis.com/Instance --output-path=gs://audit/vms.json
gcloud asset search-all-resources --scope=organizations/ORG_ID --query="labels.cost-center:*" --asset-types=compute.googleapis.com/Instance

stem: The security team wants a near real-time notification whenever the IAM allow policy of any project in the organization changes, so that an automated reviewer can check each change. Which Cloud Asset Inventory feature should they configure?

choices.text: A daily scheduled export of IAM_POLICY assets to BigQuery, with a query that compares each new snapshot with the previous day's
The asset history view, which keeps 35 days of changes and sends a notification for each change to the organization's Essential Contacts
A feed at the organization scope with the IAM_POLICY content type that publishes each change notification to a Pub/Sub topic
A search-all-iam-policies command that runs from a cron job every hour and emails the security team the complete search results

stem: An administrator enabled the Gemini Cloud Assist API in a project and granted a developer the Gemini Cloud Assist User role. The developer can chat about general topics, but questions such as "List my instances and their private interface names" return no resource details. Which change should the administrator make?

choices.text: Grant the developer the Cloud Asset Viewer role and make sure the Cloud Asset Inventory API (cloudasset.googleapis.com) is enabled in the project
Grant the developer the Organization Administrator role, because Gemini Cloud Assist reads resources only for principals who can manage IAM
Move the project into a standalone organization, because Gemini Cloud Assist analyzes resources only in organizations that have no domain
Grant the developer the Service Usage Consumer role on the project, because resource answers are billed to the API quota of each user

stem: A company's employees and contractors already sign in to all company apps through Okta. The company wants them to access the Google Cloud console and gcloud with single sign-on through Okta, without creating or synchronizing user accounts in Cloud Identity. Which approach meets this requirement?

choices.text: Configure Workload Identity Federation with a workload identity pool for Okta, then let employees impersonate a shared service account to sign in
Configure Workforce Identity Federation with a workforce identity pool at the organization and an OIDC or SAML provider for Okta, then grant roles to pool principals
Create a Cloud Identity account by hand for each employee and contractor, then turn on 2-Step Verification so that Okta passwords are reused
Install Google Cloud Directory Sync to copy Okta users into Cloud Identity every hour, then configure SAML single sign-on from Cloud Identity to Okta

stem: A company federates its users through a workforce identity pool named corp-pool. Its IdP sends a groups claim mapped to google.groups. The admin must grant the Compute Viewer role on project ops-tools to every federated user in the IdP group sre-team. Which principal identifier should the role binding use?

choices.text: principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/corp-pool/*
principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/corp-pool/group/sre-team
group:sre-team@corp-pool.iam.gserviceaccount.com
principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/corp-pool/subject/sre-team

stem: A new engineer installed the Google Cloud CLI on her laptop, ran gcloud components install kubectl, and fetched credentials for a GKE cluster. Every kubectl command now fails with an error saying that gke-gcloud-auth-plugin is not found. What should she do?

choices.text: Install the missing component with gcloud components install gke-gcloud-auth-plugin, then run the kubectl command again
Download a static service account key for the cluster and point the KUBECONFIG variable at the downloaded JSON file
Recreate the cluster with legacy client certificate authentication enabled so kubectl no longer needs any plugin
Ask an administrator to grant her roles/container.admin on the project so kubectl may use her gcloud credentials

stem: A three-person startup wants to run a dozen containerized microservices on Kubernetes. Nobody on the team wants to size, upgrade or repair nodes, and the founders want general-purpose workloads billed for the resources the Pods request rather than for whole VMs. Which GKE setup fits?

choices.text: A Compute Engine managed instance group running the containers with Container-Optimized OS and a startup script
A regional GKE Standard cluster with the cluster autoscaler enabled on three node pools of different machine types
A zonal GKE Standard cluster with node auto-repair and auto-upgrade enabled on a single e2-standard-4 node pool
A GKE Autopilot cluster, where Google manages the nodes and general-purpose Pods use the Pod-based billing model

stem: A platform team is writing an internal guide on GKE Autopilot clusters. Which statements belong in it? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Autopilot bills every Pod, including Pods that select GPUs, only for the CPU and memory that the Pod requests
Autopilot clusters can be zonal to save cost, and a zonal cluster can be converted to a regional one later on
Every Autopilot cluster is regional, with control plane replicas across multiple zones of the region you choose
Autopilot clusters can opt out of release channels so that the team decides when the control plane is upgraded
Google creates and manages the worker nodes, so you never add node pools to an Autopilot cluster yourself

stem: Six months ago a team created a zonal GKE Standard cluster in us-central1-a for its checkout service. Leadership now requires that the cluster's control plane stay available during the loss of a single zone. What must the team do?

choices.text: Update the existing cluster with gcloud container clusters update and a --region flag so it becomes regional
Add a second node pool in us-central1-b, because spreading nodes across zones also replicates the control plane
Enable node auto-repair on the existing pool, which recreates the control plane in another zone if its zone fails
Create a new regional cluster in us-central1 and migrate the workloads, since zonal clusters can't become regional

stem: Security policy says GKE nodes must not have external IP addresses. The workloads pull some images from a public registry on the internet and call a partner's public HTTPS API. Which cluster setup meets both needs?

choices.text: Create the cluster with --enable-private-nodes and set up Cloud NAT for the cluster's subnet so nodes get outbound internet access
Create the cluster with --no-enable-private-nodes and add a firewall rule that denies all ingress traffic to the node VMs
Create the cluster with --enable-private-nodes and add authorized networks, which give nodes a path to internet hosts
Create the cluster with --enable-private-nodes and rely on Private Google Access, which also routes traffic to internet hosts

stem: An engineer has an Autopilot cluster and a container image in Artifact Registry. The web app in the image listens on port 8080. She wants the app running and reachable from the internet on port 80 with as few steps as possible. Which kubectl commands should she run?

choices.text: kubectl run web --image=IMAGE --port=80, then kubectl expose pod web --type ClusterIP --port 80 --target-port 8080
kubectl create deployment web --image=IMAGE, then kubectl expose deployment web --type ClusterIP --port 8080 --target-port 80
kubectl create deployment web --image=IMAGE, then kubectl expose deployment web --type LoadBalancer --port 80 --target-port 8080
kubectl apply -f with a Deployment whose containerPort is 80, then kubectl port-forward deployment/web 80:8080 on her laptop

stem: A developer has a small Node.js web service in a local folder with no Dockerfile, and Docker isn't installed on his workstation. He wants to deploy it to Cloud Run with one command and no manual image build. What should he run, and what happens?

choices.text: gcloud builds submit --tag first, because Cloud Run accepts only images built by the user and pushed to Artifact Registry by hand
gcloud run deploy --source . so Cloud Build and Google Cloud's buildpacks build an image, store it in Artifact Registry, and deploy it
gcloud run deploy --source . so the source is copied into a Cloud Storage bucket and Cloud Run runs the files without any image
gcloud run deploy --image . so Cloud Run reads the local folder as an image and starts the code with the Node.js runtime directly

stem: A marketing team must publish a public landing page on Cloud Run. When the engineer runs gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding with --member=allUsers and --role=roles/run.invoker, the command fails because the organization enforces the domain restricted sharing constraint. What is the recommended way to make the service public?

choices.text: Ask for a project-level exception to domain restricted sharing and then retry the allUsers binding on the service again
Grant roles/run.invoker to allAuthenticatedUsers instead, because that principal type is exempt from domain restricted sharing
Put an external Application Load Balancer in front of the service, which removes the need for any invoker authorization
Disable the Cloud Run Invoker IAM check on the service, for example with gcloud run services update SERVICE --no-invoker-iam-check

stem: A Flask app runs fine on a developer's laptop, where it listens on 127.0.0.1:5000. Deployed to Cloud Run with default settings, the revision never becomes ready and the logs say the container failed to listen on the expected port. What should the developer change in the app?

choices.text: Keep 127.0.0.1 but change the port to 443 and add a TLS certificate, since Cloud Run sends requests to containers over HTTPS
Keep port 5000 and add EXPOSE 5000 to the Dockerfile, because Cloud Run sends traffic to the first port the image exposes
Listen on 0.0.0.0 on the port given by the PORT environment variable, which is 8080 unless the service sets another port
Listen on 127.0.0.1:8080, since Cloud Run's front end connects to the container through its loopback interface only

stem: A team is moving a legacy web app into a container for Cloud Run. Which statements about the runtime environment of a Cloud Run service are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: TLS is terminated by Cloud Run, so the container receives requests without TLS and doesn't need to manage certificates itself
The container can mount an NFS or Filestore share by running a mount command in its startup script, as on a Compute Engine VM
Data written to /tmp is kept on a persistent disk shared by all instances of the revision, so instances can exchange files that way
The app can use sudo inside the container to install packages at startup, because Cloud Run allows privilege escalation on demand
Files the app writes to the container's file system live in memory, count against the instance's memory, and are lost when the instance stops

stem: Each night a team must convert 2,000 image files in a Cloud Storage bucket. The work has no HTTP endpoint, each file can be handled independently, and the run should finish faster by working on many files at once. The team already has a container image that converts one slice of the files. What should they deploy?

choices.text: A Cloud Run service with a minimum of 50 instances and a script that sends one HTTP request per file to the service URL
A Cloud Run job created with --tasks set to split the work, where each task uses CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX to pick its slice
A GKE Standard cluster with a CronJob, adding a node pool sized for the peak and keeping it running between nightly runs
A Cloud Run function with an HTTP trigger that loops over all 2,000 files in a single invocation with a raised timeout

stem: A developer wrote a Python HTTP function named handle_webhook in main.py and wants it deployed as a Cloud Run function in europe-west1, built from the current directory on a Google-managed Python runtime base image. Which command matches the current Cloud Run documentation?

choices.text: gcloud run deploy handle_webhook --source . --region europe-west1, since Cloud Run reads the entry point from the service name
gcloud run deploy webhook --source . --function handle_webhook --base-image with a Python runtime --region europe-west1
gcloud run jobs deploy webhook --source . --function handle_webhook --region europe-west1 and a Python base image
gcloud run deploy webhook --image . --function handle_webhook --region europe-west1, with the folder used as the image

stem: A team deployed a Cloud Run function and is creating an Eventarc trigger so the function runs when objects are created in a Cloud Storage bucket. The trigger's service account has the Eventarc Event Receiver role and permission to invoke the function, yet trigger creation fails with a permission error about publishing to Pub/Sub. What is missing?

choices.text: The Pub/Sub Publisher role (roles/pubsub.publisher) for the project's Cloud Storage service agent, which sends the bucket's events
The Cloud Run Admin role for the Eventarc service agent, so it can redeploy the function with an event trigger attached
The Storage Object Admin role for the trigger's service account on the bucket, so it can read every new object for the function
The Pub/Sub Subscriber role for the deploying user, so the user can attach a subscription to the bucket's notification topic

stem: Users upload invoices to the bucket inv-in, located in europe-west4. A Cloud Run service must process each new invoice and each re-uploaded (overwritten) invoice exactly when it is written, but must ignore label changes on existing objects. Which settings should the Eventarc trigger use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An event filter of type=google.cloud.storage.object.v1.metadataUpdated together with an event filter of bucket=inv-in
An event filter of type=google.cloud.storage.object.v1.archived, which fires each time an object is overwritten
An event filter of type=google.cloud.storage.object.v1.finalized together with an event filter of bucket=inv-in
A trigger location of global, so the trigger can receive events from buckets in any region of the project
A trigger location of europe-west4, matching the location of the bucket that generates the events

stem: A team created an Eventarc trigger of type google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written with filters serviceName=storage.googleapis.com and methodName=storage.objects.create, targeting a Cloud Run service. The trigger shows as active and objects are being uploaded, but the service never receives an event. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Audit log triggers deliver only events from Admin Activity logs, so object writes can never be routed and a Pub/Sub trigger is required
The Cloud Run service must be made public with allUsers, since Eventarc delivers audit log events without any authentication
The methodName filter must name the HTTP verb used by the upload, such as PUT or POST, rather than the API method name
Data Access audit logs are not enabled for Cloud Storage in the project, so no audit log entry is written when objects are created

stem: A private Cloud Run service (Invoker IAM check enabled) must process every message published to the Pub/Sub topic orders. The team wants Pub/Sub to call the service directly over HTTPS without making the service public. What should they configure?

choices.text: A push subscription that uses --push-auth-service-account with an account granted roles/pubsub.subscriber on the orders topic
A push subscription to the service URL with no authentication, and the service set to accept requests from the Pub/Sub IP ranges
A push subscription to the service URL with --push-auth-service-account, and roles/run.invoker granted to that account on the service
A pull subscription on orders, with the Cloud Run service polling the subscription in a loop every few seconds for new messages

stem: A company has several teams publishing events from apps in different projects. The platform team wants one central bus that collects them, lets consuming teams subscribe through enrollments, can filter on any event attribute and can transform payloads before delivery. Which option fits?

choices.text: Eventarc Advanced, which publishes events to a central bus and uses enrollments with filtering and CEL transformations
A single Cloud Run function per producer that calls every consumer's HTTPS endpoint in turn and rewrites the payloads
Eventarc Standard, with one trigger per producer project that routes each event to every consumer's Cloud Run service
A Cloud Storage bucket per team, where producers write JSON files and consumers react through object finalized triggers

stem: A team runs an event-driven Cloud Run service that must react to messages that another team already publishes to an existing Pub/Sub topic named billing-events in the same project. They want delivery managed by Eventarc in CloudEvents format and do not want Eventarc to create a new topic. How should they create the trigger?

choices.text: gcloud pubsub subscriptions create with --push-endpoint set to the Eventarc API so Eventarc forwards each message to the service
gcloud eventarc triggers create with --event-filters="type=google.cloud.pubsub.topic.v1.messagePublished" and --channel=billing-events
gcloud eventarc triggers create with --event-filters="type=google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written" and serviceName=pubsub.googleapis.com
gcloud eventarc triggers create with --event-filters="type=google.cloud.pubsub.topic.v1.messagePublished" and --transport-topic=billing-events
